Review of 6a6f39053846ef29abbf6ca430387b545564f0de: no blocking issues

1. [non-blocking] `.github/pr-review/check.py:184`: the replacement character U+2039 `‹` is the same character that Lean uses for its assumption notation, `‹_›` (U+2039 and U+203A), which this repository's own code uses, for example at `src/Impls/Enumeration.lean:1046` (`‹_ ∈ fs›`), `src/Impls/Enumeration.lean:1422` and `src/FrenCore/Sound.lean:1109` and `:1117`. Reviews of this project often quote Lean, where `<` is common: the same line 1046 has `simp_wf) <;> (try have := ... ‹_ ∈ fs›)`, which would post as `simp_wf) ‹;> (try have := ... ‹_ ∈ fs›)`, and the reader can no longer tell which `‹` the review wrote and which the workflow put in place of `<`. A character that Lean and Fren don't use, such as U+FF1C `＜` (FULLWIDTH LESS-THAN SIGN, which no Markdown or HTML parser reads as an opener), keeps the guarantee and stays unambiguous. If you change it, change every mention together: `.github/pr-review/check.py:26`, `:66`, `:172` and `:184`; `.github/pr-review/brief.md:92`; `src/Reqs/dev/Testing.md:1187`; and the tests at `.github/pr-review/test_check.py:142`, `:143`, `:156`, `:163` and `:181`.

2. [non-blocking] `.github/pr-review/check.py:68`–`69`: the loading-tag alternative of `IMAGE` (a `<`, then optional `/` and spaces, then one of the `LOADING` words) still refuses the whole review for placeholders of the same kind as the ones whose false alarms withheld the reviews this pull request fixes. Such placeholders are the words `base`, `source`, `link`, `input`, `object`, `image`, `frame`, `track` or `meta` in angle brackets, as in a `git diff` command whose argument is `base` in angle brackets. Once every `<` becomes `‹`, no such tag can render, and an entity such as `&lt;img` renders as text, never as a tag, so in the posted comment this alternative guards nothing that the replacement doesn't already. The description says that keeping it is deliberate defence in depth, which is a fair choice. If you keep it, say in the comment at lines 64–67 that it is redundant with the replacement and kept as a second guard, and say in the brief (`.github/pr-review/brief.md:89`–`91`) that a `<` followed by one of those words withholds the review even as a placeholder. Otherwise, drop it and keep `!\[`, which the replacement does not cover. The tests that would then change are at `.github/pr-review/test_check.py:140`–`141` and `:175`–`182`.

3. [non-blocking, fix before merge] The pull request's description: the paragraph that begins "Review finding 3 concerns the comment at `.github/workflows/lint.yml:38`" describes work that is not in the diff. It mentions removing a parser dependency of `test_check.py` and restoring the comment of `requirements-test.txt`, but neither file differs from main. It also speaks of an "allowed edit scope" and of leaving something "for the user", which reads as text left over from the author's session. The comment at `.github/workflows/lint.yml:38` is accurate as main has it, since only `test_frame.py` needs the parser. Drop the paragraph so that the description matches the diff.

The change itself is sound. In CommonMark and GFM, raw HTML and autolinks both need a literal `<`, and an entity decodes to text, never to markup. So replacing every `<` in the body after `unmention` and the second `loading` check leaves nothing that can open a tag, inside code or out. The replacement cannot create an image, a URL or a mention that the checks have not seen. It also applies to the failure notes, whose `head` and `run_url` are interpolated unchecked. `problem` still refuses images, loading tags, tokens and links to other hosts, and it still reads text decoded twice. The two cases removed from the refusal list at `.github/pr-review/test_check.py:139` (an HTML comment and a closing `details` tag) are no longer refusals, and the new test at line 159 checks that they post with `‹`. The posting step in `.github/workflows/claude-review.yml:272`–`286` writes `comment.md` from `comment`'s result, both to the step summary and to the pull request, so the replaced body is what gets posted. This pull request changes no workflow, `lakefile.lean` or test driver of `pre-approval`, so that run's pass is as good as usual. The tests that this pull request adds and changes, in `.github/pr-review`, are run by the `lint` workflow, not by `pre-approval`. No bug was found, so the question of why the spec missed one does not arise.
